key_insight: The paper argues that self-evolving multimodal models can become "self-consistently wrong" if they optimize for answer agreement without forcing the decoder to use visual evidence. Its key takeaway is that improving visual reasoning requires explicitly increasing attention to visual tokens, not just making outputs more consistent.
problem_solved: It addresses visual under-conditioning in self-evolving large multimodal models: a failure mode where models rely on language priors and answer agreement instead of truly grounding predictions in the image.
method: Identifies and frames visual under-conditioning as a core weakness in current unsupervised self-evolving LMM training.
Introduces a training objective or self-evolution strategy that encourages stronger attention to visual tokens during decoding.
Keeps the setting unsupervised while improving visual grounding and reducing reliance on statistical language shortcuts.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this shows that multimodal self-improvement must be grounded in visual evidence to be reliable. It is especially relevant for building safer and more trustworthy vision-language systems that reason from images rather than memorized priors.
visual_elements: Before/after pipeline showing standard self-evolving LMMs versus visual-token-aware training

paper_title: Paying More Attention to Visual Tokens in Self-Evolving Large Multimodal Models
paper_authors: Shravan Venkatraman, Ritesh Thawkar, Omkar Thawakar, Rao Muhammad Anwer, Hisham Cholakkal
